root_causes.description: product-catalog sits on the sole shared downstream path of the user-facing frontend (frontend→product-catalog, also used by checkout and recommendation per topology). Its degraded request handling pins the frontend server-span p99 to a hard 10s ceiling across the entire window, coupled with a strong CPU burn on the catalog pods (~1.93 cores vs ~0.015 cores on frontend pods), with no errors and no restarts — a classic injected latency/CPU-saturation signature on the shared hot path.

evidence.observed_value: p50=p95=p99=max=10000.0 ms constant across the whole incident window
evidence.expected_baseline: frontend server-span p99 well under ~1000 ms; a flat 10s ceiling indicates a saturated downstream dependency
~0.015 cores observed on frontend pods — catalog pods burn ~130x more CPU, indicating saturation on the shared catalog path
error_rate < 0.01 — confirms a latency/saturation fault rather than an error abort

evidence.observed_value: no logs found (no application errors emitted by catalog)
evidence.expected_baseline: no error logs — consistent with pure latency/saturation degradation

root_causes.description: The single most anomalous raw resource signal is the catalog pods' CPU: ~1.934 cores sustained versus ~0.015 cores for frontend pods. If the injection is a CPU-stress fault on product-catalog, the CPU burn would throttle request handling and produce the 10s frontend p99 ceiling as a secondary symptom.

evidence.expected_baseline: frontend pods ~0.015 cores; catalog is ~130x hotter than peer pods

evidence.observed_value: mean=0.015 cores (p99=0.017) — frontend itself is idle in CPU terms
evidence.expected_baseline: frontend not CPU-bound, so its 10s latency originates downstream
0 — rules out pod_crash/OOM as the mechanism

root_causes.description: frontend is the user-facing victim: its server-span p99 is pinned at the 10s ceiling, but it is an aggregator with negligible CPU, so the latency is inherited from its product-catalog dependency rather than generated locally.

evidence.observed_value: p99=10000 ms for the entire window
no traces found in window (trace backend returned no long-trace samples)
evidence.expected_baseline: when healthy, frontend traces complete well under 9s

remediation_steps: Inspect product-catalog pods for injected chaos (latency/stress sidecars, pod annotations, events) and confirm the ~1.93-core CPU burn via `kubectl top pod -n otel-demo`; remove the injected fault once identified.

Verify product-catalog CPU requests/limits and check for cgroup CPU throttling; if the saturation is organic, raise limits or scale replicas, since product-catalog is the shared hot path for frontend, checkout and recommendation.
Add/adjust client-side timeouts and circuit breakers between frontend and product-catalog so a single degraded leaf cannot pin the whole frontend p99 to the 10s ceiling.
Re-measure frontend and product-catalog p99 latency after remediation to confirm the 10s ceiling is lifted and catalog CPU returns to baseline.
